newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's April retail, wholesale sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's April retail, wholesale sales rise.

text.p: Mexico's retail sales rose 6.6 percent in April compared with the same month in 1996, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) said on Friday.
INEGI said that wholesale sales in Mexico rose by 7.2 percent for the month compared to April 1996.

The figures were much better than predicted by a Reuters survey of 13 brokerages and research firms, which on average saw of a rise of 0.17 percent for retail sales and a 2.47 percent hike for wholesale sales.

INEGI said that when it calculated the difference in working days in April 1997 from April 1996, the wholesale sales rise was adjusted to about six percent. Holy Week caused less days to be worked in April 1996, whereas Holy Week fell during March this year.
It said retail sales were not affected by the difference in working days.
The INEGI report also said that purchases by wholesalers rose by 11.8 percent in April over the same month a year earlier.
Sectors that registered the greatest retail sales increase were autos, car parts, record stores, hardware, furniture, toys and gifts and department store sales, INEGI said.

Retail sales fell during the first three months of the year by 2.5 percent from the year-ago period and wholesale sales rose 1.2 percent in the time period, INEGI said in its previous report on sales levels.
